name: sapmap_models.py
summary: Core dataclasses for the SAP Landscape Attack Path Mapper: severity enum, findings, credentials, created users, forged tickets, trust relations, SAP nodes, RFC connections, SCC and BTP nodes, and the top-level SAPMAPState session container. Every model is JSON-roundtrippable via to_dict/from_dict.

name: sapmap_report.py
summary: Engagement report builder: walks an SAPMAPState once and produces both portable Markdown and a self-contained HTML deliverable with executive summary, KPI cards, SVG landscape snapshot, hardening checklist, findings, attack coverage, trust chains, credentials, SCC and BTP sections, and structured remediation.

name: sapmap_state.py
summary: Session persistence layer: saves/loads SAPMAPState to/from .sapmap JSON files in states/, maintains an RFC test cache and a created-destination log across sessions, manages the loot directory tree (secstore/hashes/tables/bia), and lists prior saved sessions.

name: sapmap_diff.py
summary: Computes a structured delta between two SAPMAPState snapshots (added/removed/changed SAP nodes, findings, RFC connections, cloud connectors, trust chains, created users) and renders the diff as Markdown or self-contained HTML matching the engagement-report visual language.

name: sapmap_findings.py
summary: Module-global findings bus that decouples the discovery and exploit modules from the GUI: any code can call emit_finding(severity, node, msg) and registered listeners receive the dict in real time, with a 60-second dedupe window and 500-entry ring buffer.

name: sapmap_gui.py
summary: Bottle HTTP backend exposing 60+ REST routes for the SAPMAP single-page app: discovery, RFC operations, exploitation, payload generation, SCC enumeration, console streaming, and session save/load. All long-running tasks run in background threads while the JS frontend polls for state updates.

name: sapmap_html.py
summary: Single self-contained 11k-line HTML/CSS/JavaScript bundle for the SAPMAP frontend: interactive SVG landscape map with pan/zoom/drag, RFC connection rendering, right-click context menus, credential dialogs, real-time console, and status bar. Exposed via the single get_html() function.

name: __init__.py
summary: Package initializer that appends every modules subpackage directory to sys.path so callers can use flat imports (e.g., `from sapmap_models import ...`) regardless of caller location.

name: sapmap.py
summary: Main CLI entry point for SAPMAP — parses arguments, launches the Bottle HTTP server, manages the pywebview GUI window (with GTK/macOS patches), and orchestrates state loading, scripted scenarios, and CLI-only scans.

name: conftest.py
summary: Pytest configuration that registers every modules subpackage directory on sys.path, mirroring the production package initializer so tests can use flat imports.

name: capture_real_ticket.py
summary: Research utility that logs into a real SAP J2EE NetWeaver instance via HTTPS form authentication, captures the MYSAPSSO2 logon ticket, decodes/parses it, and compares against a forged ticket to validate the project's ticket-forging implementation.

name: compare_with_sap_ticket.py
summary: Diagnostic tool that reads an SAP-issued MYSAPSSO2 ticket via the Gateway SAPXPG channel and compares its structure (including PKCS#7 BER fields) against a locally forged ticket to validate forging fidelity.

name: sap_betrusted_chain.py
summary: Orchestrates the Message Server betrusted + Gateway 10KBLAZE exploit chain: registers a fake internal application server via the MS internal port, then leverages the resulting trust to invoke SAPXPG OS commands without authentication.

name: sap_db_sql_writers.py
summary: Multi-database SQL execution layer for the Gateway 10KBLAZE primitive: emits per-DB (Oracle, MSSQL, HANA, MaxDB, DB2) OS command sequences that pipe SQL into the local DB client through SAPXPG.

name: sapmap_exploit.py
summary: Central exploitation orchestrator: probes Gateway vulnerability, runs 10KBLAZE OS execution, forges/uses SAP logon tickets, deploys CVE-2025-31324 webshells, creates SAPMAP users across ABAP and Java stacks, and propagates the foothold across the RFC trust graph.

name: sapmap_efspotato.py
summary: Windows LPE module that escalates to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM by coercing lsass.exe via MS-EFSRPC named-pipe authentication, complementing GodPotato on hardened hosts where DCOM unmarshalling yields only Identification-level tokens.

name: sapmap_godpotato.py
summary: Windows LPE module implementing BeichenDream's GodPotato chain — abuses SeImpersonatePrivilege via DCOM/RPCSS unmarshalling to spawn arbitrary commands as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on Server 2012-2022 and Win10-11.

name: sapmap_miniplasma.py
summary: Windows LPE module exploiting CVE-2020-17103 (cldflt.sys race) on Win10 1709+/Server 2019+ to escalate from SAP service account to SYSTEM; also exports the shared OS-exec picker and helper primitives used by GodPotato and EfsPotato.

summary: Legal disclaimer outlining intended uses, user responsibilities, no-warranty terms, responsible disclosure expectations, and licensing for the SAPMAP security research tool. Requires written authorization before use.

name: scc_config_clean_scoped.ini
summary: Test fixture representing a clean, well-scoped SCC Principal Propagation configuration with templated CN (${user_uuid}), email-domain condition, 60-minute certificate validity, and LOCAL propagation mode. Used to assert that the SCC analyzer reports no critical findings on safely scoped configs.

name: scc_config_critical_empty.ini
summary: Test fixture representing a CRITICAL-severity SCC Principal Propagation misconfiguration: empty subjectPatterns element allows any subject to be issued a short-lived certificate. Used to validate that the analyzer flags missing identity scoping.

name: scc_config_critical_name.ini
summary: Test fixture with a CRITICAL-severity SCC Principal Propagation finding: CN bound to the unscoped ${name} placeholder with no condition, allowing impersonation across users. Drives the analyzer's identity-attribute heuristics.

name: scc_config_high_email.ini
summary: Test fixture with a HIGH-severity SCC Principal Propagation finding: CN bound to ${email} without a scoping condition; email collisions or aliases enable lateral identity. Used to validate medium-strength identity binding detection.

name: scc_config_high_hardcoded_ddic.ini
summary: Test fixture with a HIGH-severity SCC Principal Propagation finding: CN hardcoded to the SAP standard user DDIC, granting any propagated session DDIC's privileges on the backend. Validates detection of hardcoded high-privilege identity binding.

name: scc_config_medium_long_validity.ini
summary: Test fixture with a MEDIUM-severity SCC Principal Propagation finding: scoped CN (${user_uuid}/OU=HR) is safe but certificateValidityPeriodInMins=1440 and ssoToleranceInHours=24 exceed recommended values. Validates time-window heuristics.

name: trustcfg_single_xsuaa.xml

name: trustcfg_xsuaa_plus_ias.xml
